Segment reductions

Source: R/numpy_indexing.R
ops_segment_sum.Rd

Ports of jax.ops.segment_sum, segment_prod, segment_max and segment_min: reduce the entries of data (along its first axis) that share a segment id. Segments without entries hold the identity of the reduction. Ids outside [0, num_segments) are dropped (negative ids do not wrap).

Usage

ops_segment_sum(
  data,
  segment_ids,
  num_segments = NULL,
  indices_are_sorted = FALSE,
  unique_indices = FALSE,
  bucket_size = NULL,
  mode = NULL
)

ops_segment_prod(
  data,
  segment_ids,
  num_segments = NULL,
  indices_are_sorted = FALSE,
  unique_indices = FALSE,
  bucket_size = NULL,
  mode = NULL
)

ops_segment_max(
  data,
  segment_ids,
  num_segments = NULL,
  indices_are_sorted = FALSE,
  unique_indices = FALSE,
  bucket_size = NULL,
  mode = NULL
)

ops_segment_min(
  data,
  segment_ids,
  num_segments = NULL,
  indices_are_sorted = FALSE,
  unique_indices = FALSE,
  bucket_size = NULL,
  mode = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Array.

segment_ids

Integer array of 0-based segment ids, one per entry of the first axis of data.

num_segments

Number of segments. NULL uses max(segment_ids) + 1, which requires concrete ids (so it cannot be used under jit()).

indices_are_sorted

Whether segment_ids is known to be sorted.

unique_indices

Whether segment_ids is known to be free of duplicates.

bucket_size

Optional size of the buckets used to group the reduction.

mode

Out of bounds mode (see lax_GatherScatterMode); the default drops.

Value

An array with leading dimension num_segments.
